answer: I would like to talk about someone who taught me a great deal in a very short time. A person I would love to work with is a former mentor of mine who now runs a successful consultancy in Dhaka, advising small businesses on strategy. I got to know him during an internship in my final year of business administration, and even in those three months I learned an enormous amount. What makes him an ideal colleague is that he is both brilliant and genuinely [[collaborative]]; he treats junior people as partners rather than subordinates. He has a way of bringing out the best in a team by giving people real [[ownership]] of their work. I remember him letting me present part of a report to a client, which was terrifying but hugely valuable. As for why I would like to work with him, I think working alongside him again would be incredibly [[stimulating]], because he constantly pushes those around him to think bigger. He is also refreshingly honest, offering feedback that is direct but never harsh. As for how I feel about the idea, it excites me, although I know I would need more experience before I could keep up with him. Honestly, I believe the people you work with shape your career more than the job itself, and he is exactly the kind of person who makes you better. Being part of a team he leads would be a genuine [[privilege]], and perhaps one day, after studying abroad, I will get that chance.

followUps.q: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
followUps.answer: It depends on the task, but generally I prefer teamwork. Other people spot mistakes I miss and bring ideas I would never think of. Working alone can feel quite [[isolating]] after a while.

followUps.q: Are you in touch with him now?
followUps.answer: Yes, occasionally. We connected on a professional networking site, and he sometimes comments on my posts. Last year he even offered to write me a reference if I apply for a master's abroad.
